article.title: Beyond Prediction Accuracy: Designing Models Around the Decision They Need to Improve
article.why: Start model design from the operational decision, economics, and causal objective rather than a benchmark metric.

paragraphs.en:
Machine-learning projects often begin with a target variable and a benchmark metric: predict purchase, maximize AUC, reduce log loss. That workflow is convenient, but it can invert the real business problem. A model is valuable because it improves a decision. Before choosing an algorithm or celebrating predictive accuracy, teams should define what action the model will change, for whom, under what constraints, and with what economic consequences.

Consider a campaign with two million eligible customers but capacity to contact only 200,000. The operational decision is not simply ‘Who is likely to buy?’ It is ‘Which 200,000 customers should receive this treatment?’ A propensity model can rank purchase likelihood, but the highest-propensity customers may already be likely to buy without contact. If the objective is incremental sales, a treatment-effect or uplift framework may be more aligned with the decision.

The loss function implied by the business can also differ from the model metric. False positives and false negatives rarely have equal costs. Contacting a customer who will not respond consumes channel capacity and campaign cost. Missing a persuadable customer sacrifices potential margin. In fraud, healthcare, or retention settings, the asymmetry can be even larger. A generic accuracy metric averages over errors without necessarily reflecting those consequences.

Capacity changes the relevant evaluation region. If only the top 5 percent can receive an offer, performance in the middle of the score distribution may have little immediate value. Teams should inspect lift, precision, expected incremental value, or profit within the actionable range. A global metric remains useful for model diagnostics, but it should not be the only acceptance criterion.

Decision timing matters too. A feature that becomes available after the campaign list is finalized cannot support the decision, even if it dramatically improves offline accuracy. Similarly, a feature that requires an unstable pipeline or several days of latency may reduce operational value. Feature availability, refresh timing, reliability, and governance belong in model design rather than being postponed until deployment.

The population must be defined with equal care. A model trained on all customers may perform well overall but poorly among the subset legally, operationally, or commercially eligible for action. If exclusions remove most high-score customers, evaluation on the unrestricted population exaggerates usefulness. Training, validation, and business simulation should therefore reflect the population on which decisions will actually be made.

Economics provides a common language for combining these elements. For each potential action, teams can estimate treatment cost, expected margin, probability of response, incremental effect, and downstream value. The optimal threshold may then be the point where expected incremental value becomes positive, subject to capacity and risk constraints. When probabilities or treatment effects are uncertain, sensitivity analysis can show how the decision changes under plausible assumptions.

Randomized experiments remain important after deployment. Offline metrics cannot fully establish whether targeting causes better outcomes. A champion model can be tested against an existing strategy using treatment and control designs that measure incremental conversion, revenue, margin, retention, and unintended effects. This closes the loop between prediction and decision quality.

Decision-centered design also improves communication. Instead of telling executives that AUC increased by 0.02, the team can explain that the new approach captures more incremental responders within the fixed contact capacity, increases expected contribution margin, or reduces wasted contacts while maintaining conversion volume. Those statements connect technical improvement with an operational mechanism.

None of this means standard predictive metrics should be abandoned. They remain essential for diagnosing ranking, probability quality, overfitting, and stability. The point is hierarchy: the business decision defines success, and model metrics provide evidence about whether the model can support that success.

A useful sequence is therefore: define the decision; define the actionable population and timing; quantify costs, benefits, and constraints; choose a modeling target consistent with the desired effect; select offline metrics that approximate decision quality; and validate the full policy experimentally where possible. Starting with the decision prevents teams from optimizing a technically impressive model that solves the wrong problem.
paragraphs.zh:
模型專案若從target與AUC開始，很容易把真正問題倒過來。模型的價值來自改善decision，因此應先定義：要改變什麼action、對誰、何時做、capacity多少、錯誤成本與經濟結果是什麼。若只能聯絡200萬人中的20萬人，問題不是單純「誰會買」，而是「哪20萬人接受施策能產生最大價值」。高propensity者可能本來就會買，因此incremental sales目的可能更適合uplift/treatment-effect。

Evaluation也要對齊actionable range與不對稱cost。只投top 5%時，中段ranking改善未必重要；offline很準但prediction時點拿不到的feature也沒有實務價值。Training/validation population應符合真正eligible population，並把latency、reliability、governance納入設計。可用expected incremental value把cost、margin、response、treatment effect與capacity整合，再透過randomized experiment驗證真正incremental outcome。標準metrics仍重要，但層級上應由business decision定義success，model metrics只是支持證據。
paragraphs.ja:
Model projectをtargetとAUCから始めると、business problemを逆向きに解くことがあります。価値はdecision改善から生まれるため、まずaction、対象population、timing、capacity、cost、economic consequenceを定義します。200万人中20万人しかcontactできないなら、「誰が買うか」ではなく「誰にtreatmentすると価値が増えるか」がdecisionです。高propensity顧客は介入なしでも購入する可能性があり、incremental salesにはuplift/treatment-effectがより整合する場合があります。

評価もactionable rangeとerror costに合わせます。top 5%だけ施策するなら中間score帯の改善価値は限定的です。prediction時点で取得不能なfeature、遅いpipeline、eligible populationと異なるvalidationも実務価値を下げます。expected incremental valueでcost、margin、response、effect、capacityを統合し、randomized experimentでincremental outcomeを検証します。標準metricは必要ですが、successを定義するのはbusiness decisionであり、metricはそのdecisionを支える証拠です。

vocabulary.usage: The workflow can invert the business problem.
AUC should not be the only acceptance criterion.
Do not evaluate only the unrestricted population.
Use sensitivity analysis for uncertain assumptions.
The point is hierarchy: decisions define success.

business.term: We should define the decision and economics before choosing the model metric.
business.explanation: 先定義決策與經濟性，再決定model evaluation。

business.term: Offline accuracy is useful only if it improves the action we can actually take.
business.explanation: 強調offline metric與實際action的連結。

sources: Decision-focused machine learning; uplift modeling; cost-sensitive classification; experimental policy evaluation.
